mcu_0160_08008bb4.name: mcu_msg_ring2_tx_step
mcu_0160_08008bb4.summary: Send the head record of message ring 2 on a free CAN1 mailbox, one frame per call

It returns 0 at once when the ring is empty. If CAN1.MSTS bit 8 (CUSS, the unit is still sending) is set it leaves the ring alone and returns the pending count. Otherwise it peeks the head record, passes it to can_message_transmit on CAN1, and advances the read index modulo 32 only when that call did not return 4, the code's no-free-mailbox result.

returns.description: 0 if the ring was empty on entry, otherwise the number of records still queued after the attempt

mcu_0160_08008bb4.notes: The name CUSS for MSTS bit 8 is from the SVD header; the meaning of the return value 4 is taken from the code.

mcu_0160_08008dc0.name: system_clock_config
mcu_0160_08008dc0.summary: Start HEXT and the PLL, switch SYSCLK to the PLL and store the resulting SYSCLK frequency
mcu_0160_08008dc0.description: System clock bring-up with the call order of the Artery demo system_clock_config: clock tree reset (crm_reset), FLASH.PSR = 0x14 (prefetch on, 4 wait states), HEXT enable and a retry loop around crm_hext_stable_wait, PLL from HEXT with multiplier code 7 (x9) through crm_pll_config, PLL enable and wait for the PLL stable flag (0x19), AHB /1, APB1 /2 and APB2 /2, auto step-up mode on, SYSCLK switched to the PLL and confirmed by reading back 2, auto step-up mode off. Finally it recomputes SYSCLK from the CRM registers, applies the AHB prescaler and stores the result in the global at 0x200000A8 (SystemCoreClock). With the 16 MHz HEXT of this board and the HEXT/2 bit clear, SYSCLK is 144 MHz.

mcu_0160_08008e30.name: mcu_block_table_load_verified

The first mismatch restarts the copy. The function returns 1 once a full pass verifies and 0 after five failed attempts, so the caller can reject a corrupt table.

mcu_0160_08009598.name: mcu_hall_position_update

It integrates the speed-scaled step (from the helper at 0x08001E0C, result at +0x64) into the electrical angle at +0x4C and wraps it modulo 0x6487E, which is 2*pi in Q16. On a sector change it snaps the angle into the expected-sector window (bounds at +0x50 and +0x54) and nudges the correction counter at +0xA4 within -0x145E..0x145E. When the byte at +0x08 is set it also smooths the angle through the Q30 low-pass step and recomputes the window through mcu_hall_sector_window_update, and the result goes to +0x44. mcu_0160_08009f40.name: mcu_pvm_init
mcu_0160_08009f40.summary: Set up the PVM on EXINT line 16, select its threshold, enable it and wait for the first event

mcu_0160_0800a0f8.name: mcu_param_record_load
mcu_0160_0800a0f8.summary: Decode the stored motor parameter record into the runtime block, rejecting blank or erased records

For a valid record the 16-bit big-endian fields at record offsets 0x02, 0x04, 0x06, 0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x3A, 0x3D and 0x83 are read with mcu_read_be16 and stored as halfwords, the values at 0x10, 0x12 and 0x14 are halved, and the fields at 0x51, 0x53 and 0x55 become floats divided by 1e6, 1000 and 1000. params.name: param_1
params.description: runtime parameter block, about 0x4E bytes of halfword and float slots

params.name: param_2
params.description: stored parameter record, validity byte at offset 0

returns.description: 0 when the record was loaded, 1 when it was rejected as blank or erased

mcu_0160_0800a0f8.notes: The physical meaning of each record field is not visible in this packet; the defaults are the values the code writes.

mcu_0160_0800a594.name: mcu_pos_tracker_init
mcu_0160_0800a594.summary: Initialise the position tracker object: range, Q15 scale, filter coefficient and gains
mcu_0160_0800a594.description: Constructor for the position tracker object used by mcu_pos_tracker_update_v143 and mcu_pos_tracker_filter_pair_step. The shift count 13 at +0x32 scales three gain constants, 0x50000, 0x30000 and 0x3D7, stored at +0x40, +0x44 and +0x48. The bounds +0x38 = 0x190000 and +0x3C = 0x147 are set, and the validity byte at +0x34 is 1 when every argument was accepted.

mcu_0160_0800ca8c.name: mcu_ratio_110_to_q15
mcu_0160_0800ca8c.summary: Return the byte at 0x20001FD3 divided by 110 in Q15, saturated at 1.0
mcu_0160_0800ca8c.description: Converts the byte at 0x20001FD3 to a Q15 fraction of 110, computed as mcu_q15_div_sat of the value shifted left 15 by the constant 0x370000 (which is 110 << 15). Values of 110 and above return 0x8000 (full scale). A zero byte returns 0.

returns.description: Q15 value of byte/110, between 0 and 0x8000

mcu_0160_0800ca8c.notes: The meaning of the scale 110 is not visible in this packet.

mcu_0160_0800cba4.name: flash_halfword_program
mcu_0160_0800cba4.summary: Program one halfword in internal flash: set PG, write, wait, clear PG
mcu_0160_0800cba4.description: SDK flash_halfword_program. It sets FLASH.CTRL bit 0 (FPRGM), writes the 16-bit value to the address, waits with flash_operation_wait_for(0x100000), and clears FPRGM. This build discards the wait status, so the function returns nothing.

mcu_0160_0800cc04.name: flash_operation_wait_for
mcu_0160_0800cc04.summary: Poll the flash status until it is no longer busy or the poll count runs out
mcu_0160_0800cc04.description: SDK flash_operation_wait_for. It calls flash_operation_status_get repeatedly while the result is FLASH_OPERATE_BUSY (0) and the poll counter is non-zero, decrementing the counter on each poll. It returns the last status, or FLASH_OPERATE_TIMEOUT (4) when the counter reaches zero.

params.name: param_1
params.description: poll count, passed in r0 by the callers (the decompiler shows the function as taking no argument)

returns.description: flash status: 0 busy, 1 program error, 2 EPP error, 3 done, 4 timeout

mcu_0160_0800cc80.name: flash_sector_erase
mcu_0160_0800cc80.summary: Erase the flash sector at an address: set SER, write FLASH.ADDR, start with ERSTRT, wait, clear SER
mcu_0160_0800cc80.description: SDK flash_sector_erase. It sets FLASH.CTRL bit 1 (SER), writes the sector address to FLASH.ADDR, sets bit 6 (ERSTRT) to start the erase, waits with flash_operation_wait_for using a large poll count, and clears SER. This build discards the wait status.

params.name: param_1
params.description: address of the sector to erase

mcu_0160_0800cd18.name: mcu_xfer_queue_init
mcu_0160_0800cd18.summary: Arm five 300-byte transfer requests and publish the table when the control pointers are set
mcu_0160_0800cd18.description: Arms five transfer request objects of 0x24 bytes starting at 0x2000212C, each with a 300-byte buffer starting at 0x200021E0, through mcu_xfer_request_arm with a repeat count of 1 and user argument 0. If the pointers at 0x200006F0 and 0x200006FC are both non-zero it stores the table in the globals 0x200027BC (base), 0x200027C0 (count 5) and 0x200027C4 (address of the 0x200006F0 control block) and returns 1; otherwise it returns 0 and publishes nothing.

returns.description: 1 when the table was published, 0 otherwise

mcu_0160_0800cd18.notes: The owner of the control block at 0x200006F0 is not visible in this packet.

mcu_0160_0800cdd8.name: mcu_can_ef00_message_send
mcu_0160_0800cdd8.summary: Send a PGN 0xEF00 message: one frame for up to 5 bytes, otherwise start a TP session
mcu_0160_0800cdd8.description: Sends a J1939 PGN 0xEF00 proprietary message. Payloads under six bytes go out as one 29-bit frame built by mcu_can_ef00_frame_build (priority 6, header bytes 1, the given header bytes, source and destination addresses), then queued with mcu_can_frame_enqueue. Longer payloads go through mcu_0160_0800d0b0 (mcu_can_tp_session_start) on the session table at 0x200027BC, using the same arguments.
mcu_0160_0800cdd8.notes: The header semantics are not documented in this packet.

mcu_0160_0800ce3c.name: mcu_limit_ratio_with_floor
mcu_0160_0800ce3c.summary: Map two values against a limit to a Q15 ratio with a 10 percent floor, saturating at full scale
mcu_0160_0800ce3c.description: Returns a Q15 derating factor. The limit comes from mcu_get_limit_min3_or_unbounded (DAT_20000660, at least 0x18000). If the limit is at or below param_1 the result is full scale (0x8000). Otherwise the larger of the two inputs is divided by the limit in Q15 and mapped to 0.9 times that ratio plus 0.1 (0x8E38 is 1/0.9 and 0xCCC is 0.1 in Q15), so the result runs from about 0.1 up to 1.0.

params.name: param_1
params.description: first input, compared with the limit

mcu_0160_0800ce3c.notes: Which physical quantities the two inputs are is not visible in this packet.

mcu_0160_0800d038.name: mcu_can_tp_rx_dispatch
mcu_0160_0800d038.summary: Route an incoming J1939 TP frame: start a session on RTS, otherwise hand it to the open sessions
mcu_0160_0800d038.description: Receive-side dispatcher for J1939 transport-protocol frames (PGN 0xEC00 TP.CM and 0xEB00 TP.DT, group with mcu_can_tp_session_start). For a TP.CM frame whose first data byte is 0x10 (request to send), it asks the accept callback at table +0x08 whether to accept, using the source and destination addresses. If accepted it finds or allocates the receive session with mcu_pair_table_find_or_alloc in mode 1 (lookup or allocate) and passes the frame to mcu_can_tp_session_handle_frame (mcu_0160_0800d1f0). Any other TP.CM or TP.DT frame goes to that handler for every 36-byte session entry in the table, counted at table +0x04. Other PGNs are ignored.

params.name: param_1
params.description: TP table header: entry base +0x00, u16 entry count +0x04, accept callback +0x08, handler callback in the entries

params.name: param_2
params.description: received CAN frame: identifier word at +0x00, first data byte at +0x05

mcu_0160_0800d038.notes: The callback signatures are taken from the code shape only.

mcu_0160_0800d0b0.name: mcu_can_tp_session_start
mcu_0160_0800d0b0.summary: Find or allocate a strict pair-table session for a multi-packet send and build its frame
mcu_0160_0800d0b0.description: Multi-packet send entry used by mcu_can_ef00_message_send for payloads of six bytes or more (group with mcu_can_tp_rx_dispatch). It finds or allocates a session for the (source, destination) pair with mcu_pair_table_find_or_alloc in strict mode (mode 0, which refuses a reversed duplicate). When it gets a session it passes the arguments to mcu_frame_build_checksum16, which fills the session frame and its repeat count and returns that result; when no session is free it returns 0 and queues nothing.

params.name: param_2
params.description: service argument, 7 at the call site from mcu_can_ef00_message_send

params.name: param_10
params.description: total to cover, passed through; 0 at the call site

returns.description: 1 when the frame was built, 0 when no session was available or a check failed

mcu_0160_0800d10a.name: mcu_can_tp_sender_step
mcu_0160_0800d10a.summary: Advance the J1939 TP sender state machine by one event: RTS, data blocks, CTS wait, end of message
mcu_0160_0800d10a.description: Sender side state machine of a J1939 transport-protocol session for PGN 0xEF00 (group with mcu_can_tp_timeout_tick and mcu_can_tp_rx_dispatch). The state byte at +0x02 selects the action. State 3 builds and sends the TP.CM request to send (mcu_can_tp_rts_frame_build), sets the timer limit to 1250 ms divided by the tick period at +0x14, and moves to state 4 (wait for CTS). States 4, 6, 7, 9 and 10 pass to mcu_0160_0800b65c (the timeout tick). State 5 sends 7-byte TP.DT frames (mcu_can_tp_dt_frame_build) from the offset at +0x0A, paced by the burst counter at +0x1A and the burst size at +0x1C. It moves to state 6 when the block end at +0x12 is reached, or to state 9 (end-of-message wait) when the total length at +0x0C is covered. Frames go out through the send callback at ops +0x0C.

params.name: param_1
params.description: TP sender session: state +0x02, id bytes +0x00 and +0x01, data pointer +0x04, offset +0x0A, total +0x0C, block end +0x12, tick period +0x14, timer +0x16, limit +0x18, burst counter +0x1A, burst size +0x1C

mcu_0160_0800d10a.notes: Several states (7, 10) only pass to the timeout tick here; their own transitions are in other code.
